text:
maya: quick spike test results — 30m soak comparing L4 / T4 / A10G for embeddings (rwk-7b-embed) and small-chat (rwk-7b-chat-small) across eu-west1 and us-west2. attaching quick summary + followups. TL;DR: A10G wins for small-chat latency P95 and tail stability, L4 gives the best embeddings throughput per GPU, T4 is cheapest per-token for big batches but has noisy P95 in eu.

zane: can you paste the exact test config (quant, kernels, batch/concurrency)? and the raw numbers? :eyes:

maya: sure — config snippet:
```
models:
  - rwk-7b-embed
  - rwk-7b-chat-small
quant: {embed: q8_0, chat: q4_0}
kernel_policy: {prefer: fused_attention, fallback: cudnn}
seq_len: {embed:256, chat:512}
batch_profile: {embed: dynamic_prefix_cache, chat: concurrency=8, max_batch=64}
regions: [eu-west1, us-west2]
soak: 30m
metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput (rps), tokens/sec, gpu_util
```

li: thanks. what packing/kv cache params did you use for embeddings? and were you using async prefix cache? we saw big gains before.

maya: embeddings used async prefix cache enabled (ttl 10m), packer target_tokens=4096, max_per_gpu 64 batches. KV cache hit ~72% after 5m in both regions.

bench-bot: summary link -> https://redwood.internal/bench/1913459999/summary (charts: latency-by-region.png, throughput-by-gpu.png)

zane: raw highlights (per single GPU, median across runs):
- Embeddings throughput (queries/sec): L4 = 5.2k rps, A10G = 4.8k rps, T4 = 2.1k rps
- Small-chat latency (p50 / p95): A10G = 18ms / 60ms, L4 = 22ms / 120ms, T4 = 28ms / 220ms
- GPU util (chat at concurrency 8): A10G 72%, L4 64%, T4 58%
- Cost rough (compute-only, $/1M tokens): T4 = $3.6, L4 = $6.1, A10G = $8.2
(we used identical model weights and the quant profiles above)

rachel: notes on kernels — enabling `fused_attention` on L4 reduced the P95 by ~35ms for chat. on T4 we frequently fell back to cudnn for some attention sizes which explains the large tail. A10G has stable fused kernels in our build so tail is much tighter. recommend enabling `kernel_policy: prefer_fused` in staging.

li: region quirks? You said eu had worse tails on T4.

maya: yes — eu-west1 T4 instances showed higher variance, likely due to noisy neighbors in that HW pool. A10G instances in eu had consistent isolation (fewer scheduler preemptions). us-west2 showed smaller gaps across GPUs. Also disk IO jitter hit models with larger swap pressure (we saw 1 spike where swap usage hit 0.6GB on T4 during heavy bursts).

zane: capacity question — if a product team wants 200k embed QPS sustained (single-token-ish queries), how many GPUs by type?

maya: back-of-envelope from measured rps/GPU above (using packing):
- L4: 5200 rps/GPU -> 200k / 5200 = ~39 GPUs (we'd recommend 45 for headroom + failover)
- A10G: 4800 rps/GPU -> ~42 GPUs (recommend 48)
- T4: 2100 rps/GPU -> ~95 GPUs (recommend 110)
These include 15% headroom and small canary buffer.

rachel: for small-chat latency-sensitive product (target p95 < 100ms) recommended infra:
- A10G Dedicated pool with kernel_policy locked + q4_0 quant for chat model. Canary with L4 fallback if cost becomes concern.

opsbot: deploy-bot: created canary pool `canary-a10g-chat-2026-03` for small-chat tests.

zane: next steps? should we run a 24h soak in eu-west1 with kernel override and q4_0 quant for chat to catch regressions?

maya: yes — planned: 24h soak (eu-west1) + 6h burst tests in us-west2, collect p50/p95, cost/dollars-per-token, and kernel_switch_count. I'll open a short PR to enable `kernel_policy: prefer_fused` in staging and schedule soak for tomorrow. adding @rachel for kernel rollout QA. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

rachel: ack — I'll add regression prompts and hook the eval alert (quality-regressions) so we don't miss output drift after quant.

maya: perfect. will paste the soak dashboards once done. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
